subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the migration delete them when the suffix scheme changes?
rationale: Config backups are a user recovery artifact and current shipped behavior keeps `.bak.1` through `.bak.4`, so deleting them on first upgrade is a compatibility and recovery-policy choice rather than a routine implementation detail.

options.title: Preserve legacy recovery points
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or convert them into the timestamped retention set before pruning anything.

options.title: Accept first-run pruning
options.body: Allow the timestamp-only scheme to delete numbered backups on first cleanup, with explicit release-note/docs coverage and acknowledgement of the recovery tradeoff.

options.title: Keep the numeric ring
options.body: Reject the timestamped naming change for now and leave the shipped numbered ring as the stable recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy recovery points
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or convert them into the timestamped retention set before pruning anything.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history and prior review context across config recovery, backup tests, and docs.
